method.kind: Visual inspection of decoded frame sheets and selected full-size frames; browser media/playback verification separately recorded.
method.presentation: Native HTML/CSS crops of decoded frames; raw video files are unaltered.
limits: No claim of watching the full clips at normal speed for pacing review.
Pull reviewed at quarter-second intervals; short faults between samples may remain.
Head and coin consecutive-frame review covers the listed intervals, not all 124 frames.
One take per scene from one model cannot establish repeatability or comparative suitability.

overall.identity_observation: Painted medium, palette and character identity broadly survive meaningful movement. Retain the direction while improving reference and contact control.
overall.reference_issue: Inner-ear marks are visible in the original shop and river starting images, as well as the generated clips. Remove those marks before a future trial.
overall.still_review_rule: Before animation, inspect believable anatomy, distinct limb/hand ownership, readable joints and support/force in the source image. Retain featureless heads and painted planes.

criteria.criterion: Full head turn with fixed front-facing torso
criteria.evidence: Head rotates between approximately 1 and 3 s; shoulders and framing remain broadly stable.

criteria.criterion: Hair/head identity and coherent turning planes
criteria.evidence: Hair silhouette remains recognizable, but central planes simplify and the contour acquires anatomy during rotation.

criteria.criterion: No facial parts or inner-ear anatomy
criteria.evidence: Inner-ear detail visible near 1.25–1.9 s; nose-like protrusion visible near 1.5–2.5 s. The late profile is cleaner. Consecutive frames 30–60 corroborate the transition.
No gross camera or lighting shift in sampled frames; subtle texture flicker not measured.

trials.next_variable: Clean featureless reference and a smooth intermediate turning contour; do not reduce the amount of head movement just to hide the failure.

trials.verdict: Strongest action prototype; reference face cleanup and finer hand control remain.

criteria.criterion: Exactly two coins transfer to child; adult finishes empty
criteria.evidence: Two discs remain readable through contact at roughly 2–3.5 s; both rest in the child palm as the adult withdraws around 3.75–5.125 s.

criteria.criterion: Continuous coin travel without disappearance or multiplication
criteria.evidence: Quarter-second samples plus all consecutive frames 42–90 show lowering, wrist roll and placement, without an observed substitution or teleportation.
Arms and hands stay attached and readable. Fine finger geometry softens/rearranges as the adult rolls the wrist; exact anatomy is not fully stable.
Loaf stays painted and broadly fixed. Window figures drift slightly. Inner-ear marks visible in the source persist; no new eyes or mouth observed in sampled full frames.

trials.next_variable: Remove ear marks in the reference; retain the clear two-disc staging and test finer hand control separately.

trials.verdict: Rise is visible, but source arm/hand anatomy is ambiguous and requires rebuilding; supporting palm also slides.

criteria.criterion: Right person rises to palm-and-knee support
criteria.evidence: Body rises from approximately 1.5–3 s, with a bent knee reaching the bank and the far leg remaining near/in the water.

criteria.criterion: Helper weight shift and pulling elbow bend
criteria.evidence: Elbow bends and the helper shifts modestly; convincing heavy exertion is less clear than the rising movement.

criteria.criterion: Continuous grip and coherent limb ownership
criteria.evidence: Contact persists through sampled frames, but that does not establish sound anatomy. Enlarged start/end pictures reveal ambiguous palm/finger ownership and an unclear helper forearm in the ending pose; the generated frame at 3 s retains the problem.

criteria.criterion: Fixed support without sliding, facial anatomy or restyling
criteria.evidence: Free palm moves uphill along the bank during roughly 1.5–3 s without a clear lift/replant. Source ear detail persists. No gross floating body or photographic restyling observed.

trials.next_variable: Rebuild the starting and ending arm/hand poses from a clearly staged figure reference before another motion test. Make both shoulder–elbow–wrist–palm chains and finger ownership legible, then test contact and counterweight.
source_pose_findings: Both submitted key poses compress the two palms, thumbs and wrapping fingers into a hard-to-read shared shape. A distinct hand for each figure cannot be confidently traced.
The ending pose hides the helper forearm in the dark sleeve; the shoulder-to-elbow-to-wrist chain reads as shortened and cramped.
The grip does not clearly depict the intended reciprocal forearm hold. Connectivity in the video preserves this source ambiguity.
The helper posture gives limited visual evidence of counterweight. This is a figure-drawing/readability critique, not a demonstration of a rescue technique.

review_revisions.trigger: User flagged strange arms and hands in the original two-person pull picture.
review_revisions.correction: Earlier coherent-limb assessment was too generous: persistent contact was mistaken for anatomically readable contact. Source pose review must precede motion review.

source_rebuild_followup.correction: The rebuilt pair was rejected after closer hand/arm review; original video review remains unchanged.
